correctness.rationale: At arbitrary integer n>=3 and m>=2, the Fourier transform of B_n(t/m) is exactly m^{1-n} times the nth power of a finite root-of-unity sum times \hat B_n. Finite translations and Zak reindexing yield the displayed normalization and phase; nontrivial mth roots give all horizontal lines, and the published unit-scale one-zero theorem rules out all remaining fibers apart from the parity-determined point. The frequency order is exactly n except where the unit factor vanishes, where it is at least n+1. 216 exact rational Laurent checks and 252 numerical root-line checks passed.

value.rationale: A complete solution of all B-spline orders n>=3 at the infinite reciprocal-integer subfamily λ=1/m addresses the explicitly unclassified higher-order small-scale Zak-zero geometry. It excludes extraneous zeros rather than simply reproducing known horizontal-line existence, provides an exact even/odd isolated-point transition, and determines generic line multiplicity. The special scale is structurally motivated by the integer-oversampling resonances in the motivating work.
